column3: Light.urban.landscape: Lighting strategies for regenerating the city
column6: This study looked at the role of public lighting in regenerating complex urban areas in order to develop a set of guidelines on how to approach urban lighting with consideration given to the wider cultural context of the city.
column9: uncovered a complex range of issues and agendas that are inherent within our central urban fabric which illustated the need for a coherent approach with which to handle them

column3: Ambulance Design for Patient Safety: towards a national ambulance fleet Future ambulances
column4: Roger Coleman; Dale Harrow; Evans Owen; Merih Kunur; Sally Halls
column6: This project investigates the developing needs of service provision and the short and long term requirements of vehicles and equipment that will be needed to address the concerns of patient and staff safety in the future in the Ambulance Service and recommends primary considerations for emergency care vehicles and equipment.
column9: there is a lack of consistency in ambulance design which reduces efficiency; there is a strong desire for standardisation in design of ambulances; the composition of ambulance fleets is changing due to improved response systems, increased care and provision of a wider range of services, leading to a requirement for three core vehicle types
column10: identified nine design challenges and expanded these into a series of performance requirements; established a three stage design direction; design ideas for the core vehicles

column3: Reading the signs: wayfinding for dementia
column6: This study looks at how residents living with dementia find their way around in Bupa care homes and makes recommendations for improving signage.
column9: signage should not be thought about in isolation but in the context of its environment including considering aspects of interior design as well as what life is like in the homes day to day
column10: a set of guidelines for designing carehomes to support residents living with dementia in finding their way around

column3: Work well: Inclusive furniture for older office workers
column6: This project found and illustrated areas of opportunity in the design of work furniture for older users and developed inclusive new concepts as exemplars that address the specific needs and desires of an ageing workforce.
column9: older workers often feel unable to change aspects of their immediate environment that are important to them, are made victims of simple usability problems, fail to use work furniture properly and maintain good work habits, are more likely to hot desk, often work outside the office in places with inadequate facilities, are adopting more mobile working habits that can have adverse consquences on their health and well-being, are interested in health issues and open to innovation in this area, are hindered in the adoption of more healthy working habits by lack of provision of amenities, see sharing knowledge as one of the key ways to connect with people in the workplace
column10: design ideas: CASTRO, a meeting table for up to five people that allows greater control over the immediate environment; AQUA, a translucent screen system for acoustic and visual control in open plan work settings; STRETCH, a series of stacking chairs that visually prompt more active working habits; NEMES, an under-desk pedestal for user customisation in hot-desking settings; HEMET, a furniture unit which supports offers working facilities for public spaces; MOTORO, a micro workstation and travel case; PRESENCE, a device for use with any task chair providing proactive healthcare information at work through simple user sensing abilities; ASAS, a circular, modular seating system for adding a multi-functional amenity area to space-restricted workplaces; PLATO, a multi-functional concept for temporary learning and teamwork settings

column3: The abilizer: aiding rehabilitation for disabled people

column10: 3 Iterative prototypes of the Abilizer concept were produced and tested with users.
column11: Financial difficulties meant that the final 3rd prototype was unable to be manufactured, meaning key features were missing for some user testing.
